name: GoodFallen
headline: One of three wallets running the same BTC 5-minute Up/Down bot, which also trades against itself across accounts. Its trades are real and its returns are steady, but no public-data rule reproduces its decisions, public-data versions lose money, and half of its income is an Obsidian-tier fee rebate.
mechanism: Trades only BTC 5-minute Up/Down markets: 252k fills in 30 days, buying both outcomes in 94% of windows at a median pair cost of 1.0125. 33% of sampled fills are maker fills. Bought shares win 1-2 points more often than their price at every price level. It shares 4,845 transactions with dangerously-skip-permissions and 1,866 with x-MoneyForWhiskas; in sampled shared transactions about a quarter are the cluster's wallets filling against each other. 30-day income: gross trading $98.9k, taker fees -$78.2k, taker rebate +$38.8k (50%), maker rebate +$3.5k.

match.detail: spot-latency taker rule: held-out AUC 0.556 vs null 0.573 (perm p=0.95), flat lag scan; directional-maker rule: AUC 0.485 (p=0.96)

backtest.detail: public-data taker rule -2.3% on traded (288 held-out windows); public-data maker -15.6% (p>0.99 for loss); the wallet's own taker buys +0.3% (p=0.41), maker fills +3.2% (p=0.10)

replicable.detail: market price beats a 1-second public spot model (Brier 0.170 vs 0.218); edge is sub-second; profit relies on cross-wallet self-trading and the 50% Obsidian rebate (at 0%: ~$24k/month)

persistence.detail: last 30 days significant (p=1e-7), no decline; depends on the Taker Rebate Program (since 2026-05-28) staying unchanged

reasons: No reverse-engineered rule matches its decisions: both the taker and maker hypotheses are at chance on held-out windows.
Rules built from public data lose money in the same windows, at any latency.
It is one of three coordinated wallets that trade against each other, and below the top rebate tier its month falls under $50k.
